lane: DENOVO (HGB-CTX) - de novo detector surface from pinned sponsor training_features only; no R0 or ancestor dots read; greedy 2.8px-spaced unit-dot emission, >3px off catalogue
hypothesis: A histogram-gradient-boosting detector on all 19 GeoDAWN band percentiles plus 11x11 neighbourhood context of the 8 gradient bands and the TRI3 concordance percentile, trained on mapped catalogue faults vs >5px off-catalogue negatives with NO distance-to-catalogue feature, ranks unmapped fault segments above the lineage emission baselines, and under spaced unit-dot emission its top 37,654 cells earn more hidden-fault credit per dot than the h19 lineage field.
mechanism: DTI credit is a per-truth-pixel max (official definition verified 2026-10-24): TPw capped at 1 per truth pixel, every non-covering unit of mass costs 0.2 in FPw. Spaced (>=2.828px) unit dots tile each trace with one 3px kernel instead of paying for a solid ridge. Context means an off-trace magnetic/gravity crest (dip/depth offset of the gradient maximum from the surface trace) can vote for the trace location, which pixel-exact concordance (E1) could not. The >3px catalogue exclusion spends zero mass on pixels the scorer masks.
named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic contacts paralleling range fronts and GeoDAWN flight-line (400 m) levelling residuals in magnetic derivatives: both correlate with mapped-fault band signatures and with strain-rate bands, so the detector may be ranking survey/contact geometry rather than unmapped Quaternary faults. The SGMC disagreement below is the current evidence consistent with this mimic.
experiments_used: 3 of 3 (E1 TRI3 0.091215, E2 SUP-logreg 0.097146, E3 HGB-CTX 0.142885 pooled HOLDOUT-DTI); no further experiments this session
